prompt.context: Our client is Busy Internet, the largest Internet Café in Ghana. Busy Internet also offers: a business incubator service, ISP (Internet Service Provider covering broadband, dial-up, satellite, and radio connection), a Copy Center, Conference Room, and Office renting. Busy Internet is experiencing a decline in profit and has hired GMA (Good Morning Africa) to assess the problems, give recommendations, and assist through the implementation process.
prompt.question: What is causing Busy Internet's decline in profit, and what recommendations would you make to address it?

clarifying_info.q: What are the major revenue-generating product lines?
clarifying_info.a: The three major revenue sources are: Copy Center, Cyber Café, and ISP.

clarifying_info.q: Have costs increased for any of the three divisions?
clarifying_info.a: Ghana experiences blackouts, and in order to maintain service Busy must use a very expensive power generator. Apart from that, the three product lines have not experienced any increase in cost.

clarifying_info.q: What do we know about revenues for the three divisions?
clarifying_info.a: The Copy Center is experiencing a decrease in revenues; the same can be said for the Cyber Café, while the ISP is slowly growing.

clarifying_info.q: What are the market trends for these three product lines in Ghana?
clarifying_info.a: Copy Center: growing market, many new small players are entering and making money. Cyber Café: internet cafés are not doing well in Ghana; many are closing as more Ghanaians enjoy home connections. ISP: growing market; technology is improving and it is now possible to reach many customers via radio.
There is a new Internet Café competitor stealing clients from Busy's Cyber Café. Competitors in the ISP space are minor players plus Ghana Telecom, the government-sponsored ISP.

clarifying_info.q: What is Busy Internet's value proposition and customer segment?
clarifying_info.a: Busy Internet targets elite customers; prices are the highest in Accra and customers expect high quality. Only one major competitor can offer similar quality in the Cyber Café space.

clarifying_info.q: Why is Busy losing Cyber Café clients?
clarifying_info.a: Clients are gradually moving to a competitor offering better customer care and service quality. Also, PCs in the café are getting old and many are not working properly, decreasing capacity and customer loyalty.

clarifying_info.q: Why are Copy Center revenues declining while the market is growing?
clarifying_info.a: Possible reasons include: quality issues (printers not competitive), poor customer service (workforce not trained), efficiency issues (old printers/copy machines break more frequently), and insufficient capacity to meet growing demand.

exhibits.title: Product Line Summary Table
exhibits.shows: A table summarizing revenue trend, cost trend, market trend, and Busy's competitive position for each of the three product lines: Copy Center, Cyber Café, and ISP
exhibits.data: Copy Center: Revenues declining, Cost stable, Market growing, Position average player; Cyber Café: Revenues declining, Cost stable, Market declining, Position major player; ISP: Revenues growing, Cost stable, Market growing, Position major player

framework: Identify the product mix and segment revenues by division (Copy Center, Cyber Café, ISP)
Analyze revenues vs. costs separately for each division
Assess market trends for each product line (growing, stable, or shrinking)
Understand competitive dynamics and Busy's positioning per segment
Diagnose root causes of revenue decline in Copy Center and Cyber Café
Formulate recommendations prioritized by market opportunity and strategic fit
Consider implementation challenges specific to Ghana's business environment

questions.prompt: Why is the Cyber Café revenue declining?
questions.guidance: The decline is volume-driven, not price-driven. Busy is losing customers to a competitor with better customer care and newer equipment. PCs are aging and many are non-functional, reducing effective capacity and loyalty. The overall Cyber Café market in Ghana is also contracting as home internet adoption grows.

questions.prompt: Why is the Copy Center revenue declining despite a growing market?
questions.guidance: A strong candidate investigates multiple hypotheses: (1) quality — printers are not competitive; (2) customer service — workforce untrained; (3) efficiency — aging machines break frequently, reducing throughput and loyalty; (4) capacity — Busy may not have invested to meet rising demand. The declining Cyber Café traffic is also a contributing factor as footfall decreases.

questions.prompt: What is the overall profit driver diagnosis? Summarize in an executive framework.
questions.guidance: The profit decline is primarily revenue-driven, not cost-driven. Costs have remained stable across all three divisions (aside from the generator expense from blackouts). Both the Copy Center and Cyber Café are losing volume. The ISP is the one bright spot with growing revenues in a growing market.

brainstorming.prompt: What are possible reasons that Copy Center revenues are declining even though the overall market is growing?

categories.name: Quality
ideas: Printers are old and produce inferior output vs. newer competitors

categories.name: Customer Service
ideas: Poor service attitude driving customers to competitors

categories.name: Operational Efficiency
ideas: Old equipment breaks frequently, reducing available capacity
Downtime from blackouts not adequately covered by generator for copy machines

categories.name: Capacity
ideas: Busy has not scaled copy capacity to meet growing market demand
Competitors have added more machines and taken market share

categories.name: Cross-traffic dependency
ideas: Declining Cyber Café footfall reduces Copy Center walk-in customers
No targeted marketing for Copy Center as a standalone service

recommendation: Invest in the Copy Center: it is a growing market where Busy can recover lost share by upgrading equipment, training staff, and adding capacity
Maintain the Cyber Café but do not pursue major expansion: the market is declining, but the café serves as a cross-selling channel for ISP and Copy Center services
Aggressively grow ISP: leverage existing client portfolio and economies of scale; use radio technology to expand reach and outpace minor competitors before Ghana Telecom strengthens
Invest in customer care and technology upgrades across all divisions (especially Cyber Café PCs) to restore loyalty and differentiation among elite customers
risks: Shareholders may resist additional investment without clear ROI evidence; Estelle (the MD) is skeptical of technology and customer care spend
Implementation in Ghana is challenging: information gathering is difficult, managers may flood consultants with irrelevant data, and cultural resistance to change is strong
Ghana Telecom as a government-backed ISP competitor could receive preferential treatment or pricing power
If Cyber Café decline accelerates faster than expected, cross-selling benefits may not materialize
next_steps: Conduct customer surveys and competitive benchmarking for the Cyber Café to quantify lost clients and willingness-to-pay for improved service
Audit Copy Center equipment age and downtime rates; build business case for upgrade investment
Model ISP revenue growth scenarios using radio-reach expansion
Develop a change management plan addressing stakeholder buy-in, especially the MD and department managers, accounting for Ghana-specific organizational dynamics
